functions.signature: float SpringDamperFloat(FAlsSpringFloatState& SpringState, float Current, float Target, float DeltaTime, float Frequency, float DampingRatio, float TargetVelocityAmount = 1.0f)
functions.note: The Python call does NOT mutate the passed state struct; it returns (value, new_state). state_in / state_out are the FAlsSpring*State fields (Velocity, PreviousTarget, bStateValid). C++: DeltaTime <= UE_SMALL_NUMBER returns Current and leaves the state untouched; an invalid state returns Target, zeroes Velocity, stores PreviousTarget=Target and sets bStateValid; otherwise FMath::SpringDamper is run with TargetVelocity = (Target - PreviousTarget) * Clamp01(TargetVelocityAmount) / DeltaTime.

functions.signature: bool TryCalculatePoleVector(const FVector& ALocation, const FVector& BLocation, const FVector& CLocation, FVector& ProjectionLocation, FVector& PoleDirection)
functions.note: out = [bool, ProjectionLocation, PoleDirection]. Editor Python returns None when the C++ function returns false, so in the false cases the two out vectors are NOT observable and are stored as null. C++ semantics for the false cases (from the source): A==B (|AB| nearly zero, tolerance 1e-4) -> ProjectionLocation=A, PoleDirection=0; A,B,C collinear (the normalized pole direction cannot be built, |B - Projection|^2 < 1e-8) -> ProjectionLocation = A + AB projected on AC, PoleDirection = unnormalized B - Projection. A==C (AC cannot be normalized) returns true with ProjectionLocation=A and PoleDirection=normalized AB.
